title: Free, open-source NotebookLM alternative with any AI · {name}
description: A free, open-source alternative to NotebookLM, now Gemini Notebook: answers from your files with any AI, cited by the passage. Your files stay on your devices.
h1: An open-source alternative to NotebookLM, with any AI and your files on your devices
acts: with any AI and your files on your devices
lede: NotebookLM, which Google now calls Gemini Notebook, answers from your sources with Gemini, in your Google account. {name} answers from your files with the AI you choose, Mistral, Claude or one on your own computer, cites the passage it read, and keeps the files on your devices. Free and open source.
cta2: Get the AI on this computer
facts: Any AI, a local one included
fair.title: NotebookLM, fairly
fair.body: NotebookLM, which Google renamed Gemini Notebook in July 2026, answers from the sources you give it: PDFs, Google Docs and Slides, web pages, YouTube videos, audio. Each answer cites the passage it came from, and a click opens it there. From the same sources it makes Audio Overviews, discussions between AI hosts in more than 80 languages, and videos, mind maps, flashcards, quizzes and slide decks. It is free to start with a Google account, with 100 notebooks of 50 sources each. Google says your data is not used to train it unless you send feedback.

table.rows: Any: on this computer, a free one, your key, your plan. Mistral, Claude and ChatGPT among them.
Gemini, Google’s own. Its pages offer no other.
On your devices, in the browser, encrypted. No {name} server keeps them in a form it can read.
With the service, in your Google account: it keeps a copy of each source you add.
The AI you choose. With the AI on this computer, nobody.
Google. Not used to train it unless you send feedback; then people at Google may review what you sent, which is kept up to 3 years.
By the passage: a number opens the file at the words it read, lit. Double-check then compares each claim with its source.
By the passage too: a citation opens the quote in its source.
PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, CSV, text, pictures, recordings, whole folders, and the sites you allow.
PDF, Word, PowerPoint, text, Google Docs, Slides and Sheets, web pages, YouTube videos, audio, pictures, ePub. Up to 500,000 words or 200 MB a source.
Ask for a summary, a quiz, a mind map or a timeline: each stays in the task. A child gets a profile a parent sets.
Flashcards, quizzes, mind maps and study guides, one click each, and a Learning Guide way of answering.
Answers read aloud, in a voice made on your device. No Audio Overviews.
Audio Overviews in more than 80 languages. Joining the discussion yourself works in English only.
{name} is free; the AI may not be.
Free within standard limits. More with Google AI Plus at $4.99 a month, Pro at $19.99, or Ultra from $99.99.
Yes, MIT. Anyone can read every line.
Google’s pages offer no source code.
Plain files and backups. ChatGPT’s, Claude’s and Gemini’s exports come in.
Notes export to Google Docs, and what it makes downloads piece by piece. Its help describes no export of a whole notebook or of a chat.
better.title: Where NotebookLM does better
better.items: Audio Overviews: your sources as a discussion between AI hosts, to listen to or download. {name} reads an answer aloud in one voice, and makes no such programme.
Video Overviews and infographics of your sources. {name} makes slides, charts and diagrams, not a film of your documents.
Flashcards and quizzes one click away, which remember how far you got. In {name} you ask for a quiz or a mind map, and it makes one.
It reads a YouTube video by its transcript, and a Google Doc as it changes.
One Google account and your notebooks are on every device, with phone apps. {name} has them only on the devices you add, one by one.
both.title: Use both
both.cards: Payslips, medical letters and contracts with the AI on this computer; the course you want to listen to with NotebookLM.
A second opinion on the same sources
Drop the same files in {name} and ask Mistral or Claude what Gemini answered. Each cites the passage, so you can check both.
Download its reports and slide decks, drop the files in {name} with your sources, and carry on from there.
catch.items: No Audio Overviews, and no videos of your sources. {name} reads an answer aloud, in one voice.
{name} is free; the AI behind it may not be.
Without a sign-up, only the AI on this computer answers. It needs 12 GB of memory and a recent graphics chip, and no phone runs it.
With an AI online, the passages a request needs go to that AI. Only the AI on this computer keeps everything at home.
Your work lives in this browser. Clear its data without a backup and it’s gone.
A notebook doesn’t come in whole: bring its sources and the files it made.
faq.items: Is there a free, open-source alternative to NotebookLM?
{name} is free and under the MIT licence. It answers from your files with any AI and cites the passage it read. The AI on this computer costs nothing.
Yes. Google renamed it in July 2026 and says it is the same product, with existing notebooks still there.
Can it turn my documents into a podcast, like Audio Overviews?
No. {name} reads an answer aloud in one voice, made on your device. For a discussion between hosts, NotebookLM is the tool.
Can I use it for studying?
Yes. Give it your course and ask for a summary, a quiz, a mind map or a timeline; each answer cites the page it came from. A child gets a profile a parent sets, with no account.
Can I use Mistral, or keep everything in Europe?
Yes. {name} is made in France and open source, and its AI can be European too: Mistral’s with your key, or one on your own computer.
Does it read Word, Excel and PowerPoint files?
Yes, as they are, and PDFs, pictures and whole folders. It hands back Word and Excel files too.
And Tasks, Gemini’s mode that does the work?
That is another part of the Gemini app, with a page of its own: {compare-gemini-tasks}.
end.title: Give {name} a file, and ask where it says so
